How confidence is setIt follows the kind of evidence, not judgement.
  • The customer's own statement (high confidence at most): The organisation says so itself: its press release, website, annual report or a named executive on the record.
  • Regulatory or securities filing (high confidence at most): A filing by the customer or the vendor names the relationship.
  • Independent press (high confidence at most): Editorially independent reporting describes the deployment.
  • Joint announcement (medium confidence at most): A press release issued with the vendor, usually with a quote from the customer.
  • Vendor case study (medium confidence at most): The vendor's published customer story naming the organisation.
  • Vendor mention only (low confidence at most): A logo, a customer list or a passing mention by the vendor, with nothing from the customer.
  • An organisation that also holds a stake in the vendor is labelled “Investor and customer” and is never rated above medium.
  • A partnership is listed as a partner, not a customer.

Sanctions and export controlsThe US Department of Defense published a notice on 2026-06-10 (91 FR 35189) designating Alibaba Group Holding Limited a Chinese military company under Section 1260H of the FY2021 National Defense Authorization Act; a removal notice published on 2026-11-10 concerned a different company. Alibaba's 20-F filed on 2026-05-20 disclosed an earlier listing in February 2026 that was withdrawn, and stated that the designation mainly prohibits the Department of Defense from business dealings with listed entities and does not trigger blocking sanctions. The South China Morning Post reported on 2026-10-29 that a US court granted Alibaba a preliminary injunction limited to a related lobbying restriction and that the designation remains in place while Alibaba's challenge continues. Alibaba Group and Alibaba Cloud entities were not found on the US Consolidated Screening List (which includes the Entity List, SDN List and the Chinese Military-Industrial Complex Companies list), the UK Sanctions List, the EU consolidated financial sanctions list or Canada's consolidated autonomous sanctions list in files downloaded on 2026-11-20. The 20-F also states that US export controls restrict the group's access to advanced AI chips. No restriction on the use of Alibaba Cloud or Qwen issued by a government body in Canada, the UK or the EU was found. Reputation

Questions to ask the vendor (5)

  1. In what year was the Alibaba Cloud business established, and which legal entities operate it today?
    Company age indicates operating track record.
  2. Has Alibaba Cloud made any workforce reductions in the last 24 months, and how many staff work on Model Studio and Qwen?
    Workforce reductions can affect support and product continuity.
  3. What security incidents affecting Alibaba Cloud customer data have occurred in the last 24 months, and how were customers notified?
    Past security incidents and their handling indicate control maturity.
  4. Have any international enterprise or public-sector customers ended their use of Alibaba Cloud in the last 24 months because of the Section 1260H designation or other regulatory concerns?
    Loss of large customers can indicate product or trust problems.
  5. Have there been any departures, investigations or disputes involving the leadership of Alibaba Cloud in the last 24 months?
    Leadership instability or misconduct affects vendor reliability.

Timeline

  1. 2026-11-16 · launch Alibaba Cloud
    Alibaba releases Qwen4-Max flagship model

    Alibaba announced Qwen4-Max on 2026-11-16, describing it as the most capable Qwen model so far, with native vision and a one-million-token context window, available through QwenCloud's Token Plan and API. A follow-up Alibaba Cloud post on 2026-11-17 presented the model to enterprise teams. Neither post named Model Studio as a launch channel, and Alibaba said smaller open-weight Qwen4 models would follow without giving a date. Alibaba Cloud (vendor, retrieved 2026-11-22, opens in new tab)Alibaba Cloud (vendor, retrieved 2026-11-22, opens in new tab)

  2. 2026-11-13 · litigation Alibaba Cloud
    Anaconda files copyright case naming Alibaba Group and Alibaba Cloud in Delaware federal court

    According to the federal docket index published by CourtListener, Anaconda, Inc. filed a copyright case against Alibaba Group Holding Limited in the US District Court for the District of Delaware on 2026-11-13 (No. 1:26-cv-01466), with Alibaba Cloud listed among the parties. The claims and any response were not reviewed. Free Law Project (CourtListener RECAP archive of US federal court dockets) (primary filing, retrieved 2026-11-20, opens in new tab)

  3. 2026-10-26 · litigation Alibaba Cloud
    US court grants Alibaba a preliminary injunction limited to a lobbying restriction; designation stands

    Reported by the South China Morning Post on 29 October 2026: a judge of the US District Court for the Northern District of California granted Alibaba a preliminary injunction against a lobbying restriction tied to its Section 1260H designation, in a lawsuit Alibaba filed on 23 June 2026, and did not decide Alibaba's challenge to the designation itself, which remains in place. The Next Web reported on 5 July 2026, citing Bloomberg, that the court had earlier granted temporary relief on the same restriction. South China Morning Post (carried by The Star) (independent press, retrieved 2026-11-20, opens in new tab)The Next Web (independent press, retrieved 2026-11-20, opens in new tab)

  4. 2026-09-08 · regulatory action DeepSeekAlibaba Cloud
    US agencies' advisory alleges model distillation campaigns by DeepSeek, Alibaba and four other firms

    CISA, the NSA and the FBI published advisory AA26-251A on 8 September 2026, which stated that DeepSeek, Moonshot AI, Alibaba, MiniMax, StepFun and Z.AI had conducted high-volume distillation of US AI companies' models since at least late 2024 in breach of the providers' terms of use. The advisory stated that DeepSeek used the outputs to train its R1 and V3 models and that Alibaba used them to improve its Qwen models. These are the agencies' allegations; no response from either company was found in this session. Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency, with NSA and FBI (regulator or standards body, retrieved 2026-11-20, opens in new tab)

  5. 2026-06-10 · regulatory action Alibaba Cloud
    US Department of Defense designates Alibaba Group Holding Limited a Chinese military company

    The US Department of Defense published a notice in the Federal Register on 10 June 2026 under Section 1260H of the FY2021 National Defense Authorization Act that lists Alibaba Group Holding Limited as a Chinese military company, stating that it is indirectly affiliated with China's state assets regulator and is a military-civil fusion contributor through affiliation with the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology. Alibaba's annual report filed on 20 May 2026 disclosed that an earlier listing in February 2026 had been withdrawn and stated that the designation mainly prohibits the Department of Defense from dealing with listed entities and does not trigger blocking sanctions.
